channel.title: Bola Pádel
channel.description: Bola Pádel: pro padel tour news, opinion, podcast and a weekly newsletter.

item.title: Garrido and De Pascual beat Stupaczuk and Sanz to reach the Dubai P1 semi-finals
item.description: A year after his last semi-final, also in Dubai, Javi Garrido is back in one. With Juani De Pascual, who at 21 plays his first in Premier.

item.title: Lebrón and Augsburger beat Víctor Ruiz and Rodrigo and will face Arce and Tello
item.description: With Coello and Tapia and Galán and Chingotto missing, they're the highest-ranked pair at the Dubai P1. On Friday, in the quarter-finals, the Kuwait finalists.

item.title: Roglan and Aragón come back against Paquito and Di Nenno and reach the last 16 in Dubai
item.description: They came through qualifying and lost the first set 6-0 to the fourth seeds. They won 0-6, 6-4, 6-2. It's their first Premier last 16 together.

item.title: Coello and Tapia pull out of the Dubai P1 after an injury to Tapia
item.description: Agustín Tapia is injured and the world number ones won't play in Dubai, where they were going for a third straight title. A lucky loser pair will take their place in the draw.

item.title: Why saving Coello for the third point made sense
item.description: Before the World Cup final, a lot of people couldn't understand why Juanjo Gutiérrez kept Coello for the last match. I could. I wrote it in a WhatsApp message and never said it here.

item.title: Spain, world champions, give all the credit to Juanjo Gutiérrez
item.description: Coello, Lebrón and Paquito said it in the Doha press room: the head coach's decisions shaped the final. Paquito, who is saying goodbye to the national team, started by thanking him.

item.title: Spain beat Argentina in both World Cup finals in Qatar
item.description: The men won 2-1 and ended Argentina's run as 2022 and 2024 champions. Coello and Nieto sealed the final. The women won 2-0: a seventh straight World Cup.

item.title: Spain win the women's World Cup in Qatar for a seventh title in a row
item.description: Ari Sánchez and Andrea Ustero beat Osoro and Fassio 6-3, 6-3. Paula Josemaría and Gemma Triay sealed the 2-0 against Brea and Jensen: 6-2, 6-7, 6-3. A tenth World Cup for Spain.

item.title: Italy beat France for a fourth straight bronze at the women's World Cup
item.description: Italy's women beat France 2-0 in the third-place match. Bronze in 2021, in 2022, in 2024 and now again in Doha.

item.title: Spain and Argentina will meet in both World Cup finals in Qatar
item.description: Spain beat Portugal 2-0 and the women beat France 2-0. Argentina beat Italy 2-0 in both draws. On Saturday, a double final in Doha, just like 2021 and 2024.

item.title: Spain and Argentina put both their teams into the World Cup semi-finals in Qatar
item.description: Spain beat Brazil 2-0, with Coello and Javi Leal on the same side, and Argentina beat Germany 3-0. The women, two more 3-0s. They can only meet in Saturday's finals.

item.title: Spain are through to the World Cup quarter-finals in Qatar and Tapia wins on his debut
item.description: Spain beat Paraguay 3-0, with Javi Leal making his debut, and are sure of a place in the last eight. Argentina beat the Netherlands 3-0 in Tapia's first match. The women, two more 3-0s. The groups finish today.

item.title: Spain and Argentina start the World Cup in Qatar with a 3-0
item.description: Argentina dropped three games in three matches against Australia. Spain beat Sweden, with a scare in Yanguas and Goñi's match. The women also started with clean sweeps. Today, Paraguay and the Netherlands.

item.title: Where to watch the World Cup in Qatar on TV and streaming
item.description: Movistar Plus+ in Spain and Andorra. ESPN across the Americas. Red Bull TV, free, almost everywhere else. And the FIP's YouTube channel for whatever TV doesn't show.

item.title: These are the groups for the World Cup in Qatar
item.description: Argentina, the champions, with France, Australia and the Netherlands. Spain, with the UAE, Sweden and Paraguay. The Spanish women, with Brazil, Germany and Great Britain. It starts tomorrow in Doha.

item.title: Gemma Triay is now the player with the most titles in padel history
item.description: The Kuwait Major takes her to 59. Three players arrived level on 58: Ale Salazar, Ari Sánchez and her. The final, against Ari, decided who would stand alone.

item.title: Coello and Tapia win the Kuwait Major and will finish 2026 as number one
item.description: 6-1, 6-1 over Arce and Tello in 55 minutes. With the title, no one can catch them in the Race. It's their fourth straight year on top. In the women's final, Triay and Brea came from behind against Ari Sánchez and Andrea Ustero.

item.title: Arce and Tello will face Coello and Tapia in the Kuwait final; Ari and Andrea take on Triay and Brea
item.description: A week ago, Arce and Tello lost a final in Melilla. Today they play a Major final. Ari Sánchez and Andrea Ustero come through a semifinal of more than three and a half hours. Against Triay and Brea it's six wins each this year.

item.title: Javi Leal replaces Galán at the World Cup in Qatar
item.description: The Spanish Padel Federation announced it on Friday, hours after Ale Galán pulled out. Javi Leal, 23 and world number 16, will play his first World Cup.

item.title: Ale Galán will miss the World Cup in Qatar through injury
item.description: The Spanish Padel Federation announced it on Friday. After missing the Kuwait Major, Galán won't be in Doha either. The World Cup starts on Monday.

item.title: Aimar Goñi will play his first Major semifinal before heading to the World Cup with Spain
item.description: With Edu Alonso, 6-1, 6-2 against Stupaczuk and Sanz, the fourth seeds. Today, in Kuwait, against Tello and Arce. Next week, Goñi plays the World Cup.

item.title: Libaak and Alfonso beat Lebrón and Augsburger again and will face Di Nenno and Navarro
item.description: They had already beaten them in Madrid. Yesterday, in Kuwait, they did it again: in the third set, Lebrón and Augsburger won just one game. Sintes and Zamora are also into the quarterfinals. Yanguas and Nieto are out.

item.title: Lebrón and Augsburger beat Abud and Belluati and will face Libaak and Alfonso
item.description: The qualifiers' run is over. Coello and Tapia, in under an hour, and Yanguas and Nieto, in three sets, are also into the round of 16. Today, Augsburger faces his national team partner.

item.title: Sintes and Zamora beat Momo and Campagnolo and will play their first Major round of 16
item.description: Between them they are 38 years old. They were one game from losing and won the next three. On Wednesday, in Kuwait, they play their first round of 16 at a Major.

item.title: Abud and Belluati come back in Kuwait and will face Lebrón and Augsburger
item.description: They came through qualifying, lost the first set and turned it around. It's Martín Abud's first main-draw win at a Major. On Tuesday, the third seeds.

item.title: Chingotto and Galán pull out of the Kuwait Major after an injury to Ale Galán
item.description: Ale Galán is injured and the second-ranked pair won't play in Kuwait. The very place where, a year ago, they won the first FIP World Cup Pairs.

item.title: Hexagon leaves Madrid: four venues, eight teams and goodbye to sets
item.description: The Hexagon Cup becomes the Hexagon World Series. In 2027 it starts in Madrid and ends in Abu Dhabi, with eight teams and a format with no games or sets: best of five super tie-breaks.

item.title: These are Argentina's 16 for the World Cup in Qatar
item.description: Eight men and eight women. The men are defending the title and going for a third in a row. The women want revenge after two finals lost to Spain.

item.title: These are Spain's 16 for the World Cup in Qatar
item.description: Eight men and eight women. From 2 to 7 November, in Doha. The men want back a title they haven't won since 2021. The women are going for a seventh in a row.

item.title: Augsburger and Libaak launch their own brand with Siux
item.description: Two Argentinians from Siux, two new logos in one week. Leo Augsburger now signs as "Laugsburger". Tino Libaak does it with three letters: TLK.
